suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add a note under Coding Conventions: 'When computing aggregate throughput for concurrent benchmarks, use wall clock time as denominator: total_tokens / wall_clock_seconds. Do NOT use sum(per-request decode times) which gives per-user throughput regardless of concurrency. Verify: aggregate at concurrency=N should be approximately N × concurrency=1 value.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: coding_agent_bench.py had this exact bug (originally reported as blocking in round 1 review). The original run-baseline-benchmarks worker (skillFeedback.followedProcedure=true) did not notice the issue. Aggregate throughput verification against expected scaling is a simple sanity check that would catch this class of bug.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add two validation steps: (1) After creating benchmark scripts, verify that aggregate throughput at concurrency=2 is approximately 2x the concurrency=1 value. If not, the aggregation formula is wrong. (2) Before running benchmarks with a new model, check model config.json for max_position_embeddings and set --max-model-len accordingly to avoid validation errors.
